title: Generators
description: Learn about generators and lazy evaluation in Python.
learning_objectives: Understand generator functions and the yield keyword.
Grasp lazy evaluation and its memory trade-offs.

sections.title: What is a Generator?
sections.learning_objective: Understand the concept of a generator.
sections.markdown: A generator is a special type of iterator that allows you to iterate over a sequence of values without storing them all in memory at once.
key_points: What is a Generator? is a core concept to understand
Practice applying What in real code

sections.title: The Yield Keyword
sections.learning_objective: Learn how to use the yield keyword.
sections.markdown: The `yield` keyword is used in generator functions to return a value and pause execution until the next value is requested.
key_points: The Yield Keyword is a core concept to understand
Practice applying The in real code

sections.title: Generator Function vs List
sections.learning_objective: Compare generator functions to standard functions returning lists.
sections.markdown: A standard function computes all results and returns a list. A generator function computes one result at a time, saving memory.
key_points: Generator Function vs List is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Generator in real code

sections.title: Generator Expressions
sections.learning_objective: Use generator expressions for concise syntax.
sections.markdown: Generator expressions are similar to list comprehensions but use parentheses instead of square brackets. This is a concise way to create generators.
key_points: Generator Expressions is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Generator in real code

sections.title: Lazy Evaluation
sections.markdown: Generators use lazy evaluation, meaning they generate values only when needed rather than upfront. This drastically reduces memory consumption.
key_points: Lazy Evaluation is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Lazy in real code

sections.title: Send and Throw Awareness
sections.learning_objective: Be aware of advanced generator methods.
sections.markdown: Generators have send awareness; you can send data into a generator using `.send()`. You can also raise exceptions inside them using `.throw()`.
key_points: Send and Throw Awareness is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Send in real code

sections.title: Memory Trade-offs
sections.markdown: While generators save memory, they can be slower to access repeatedly since memory trade-offs favor low footprint over speed for multiple traversals.
key_points: Memory Trade-offs is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Memory in real code

sections.title: Common Uses
sections.markdown: Generators are commonly used for reading large files, generating infinite sequences, and handling streaming data efficiently.
key_points: Common Uses is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Common in real code

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.markdown: A common mistake is trying to iterate over a generator multiple times. Once exhausted, it yields nothing and must be recreated.
key_points: Common Mistakes is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Common in real code

sections.title: Interview Points
sections.markdown: Interviewers often ask about the difference between `yield` and `return`, and how generators help with memory management in large datasets.
key_points: Interview Points is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Interview in real code
